newsitem.title: NORWAY: Winners of Nobel Peace Prize since 1970.
newsitem.headline: Winners of Nobel Peace Prize since 1970.

text.p: Following are the winners of the Nobel Peace Prize since 1970:
1970 - Norman Borlaug, International Maize and Wheat Improvement Centre, Mexico City.
1971 - West German Chancellor Willy Brandt, architect of "Ostpolitik" policy aimed at detente with eastern Europe.
1972 - No prize given.
1973 - Shared by U.S. Secretary of State Henry Kissinger and North Vietnamese peace negotiator Le Duc Tho, for talks on ending the Vietnam War (Tho declined the prize).
1974 - Shared by Japanese Prime Minister Eisaku Sato and Sean MacBride, president of the International Peace Bureau in Geneva and the Commission of Namibia at the United Nations in New York.
1975 - Andrei Sakharov, dissident Soviet physicist and human rights campaigner.
1976 - (Prize reserved but awarded in 1977) Shared by Betty Williams and Mairead Corrigan, leaders of the "Peace People" movement to end sectarian violence in Northern Ireland.
1977 - Human rights watchdog Amnesty International.
1978 - Shared by Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin.
1979 - Mother Teresa of Calcutta.
1980 - Argentine human rights campaigner Adolfo Perez Esquivel.
1981 - Office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees.
1982 - Shared by Sweden's Minister for Disarmament Alva Myrdal and Mexican diplomat and former foreign minister Alfonso Garcia Robles.
1983 - Lech Walesa, leader of Poland's Solidarity union.
1984 - Desmond Tutu, head of Anglican Church in South Africa and anti-apartheid campaigner.
1985 - International Physicians for the Prevention of Nuclear War, led by Yevgeny Chazov of the Soviet Union and Bernard Lown of the United States.
1986 - Elie Wiesel, Jewish author and human rights campaigner.
1987 - Costa Rican President Oscar Arias, author of a peace plan for Central America.
1988 - U.N. Peacekeeping Forces.
1989 - The Dalai Lama, exiled spiritual and political leader of Tibet.
1990 - Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.
1991 - Detained Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi.
1992 - Rigoberta Menchu, Guatemalan campaigner for Indian human rights.
1993 - African National Congress leader Nelson Mandela and South African President F.W. de Klerk.
1994 - Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, Foreign Minister Shimon Peres and PLO chairman Yasser Arafat.
1995 - Veteran anti-nuclear campaigner Joseph Rotblat and his Pugwash organisation.
1996 - East Timor campaigners Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Felipe Belo and Jose Ramos-Horta.
